studies.title: Read In His Name
studies.meaning: The first word is an imperative to read, and it is given without an object, so what is to be read is not specified. It is qualified instead: read in the name of your Lord. Then two lines about creation and two about teaching, arranged as a pair. What was made is a human being from something clinging; what was taught came through a pen and covered what a person did not know. The last line names ignorance as the starting condition.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, and the sources agree with unusual firmness that these are the first ayat of the Quran, received in a cave outside Mecca. The account is well attested: the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was alone, was told to read, answered that he could not, and the exchange was repeated before these lines were given. He returned home shaken and was covered until it passed.

keyTerms.note: The verb covers reading from a text and reciting from memory, and it has no object here. The root also gives the name of the Book itself, so the first word spoken names what would follow.
From a root meaning to hang or attach, the same root behind the word for a leech. The human origin is named by how it held on rather than by what it was made of.
A superlative used of God only here in the Quran. It arrives attached to the second command to read, so the generosity being named is specifically the giving of what follows: teaching.
The reed used for writing. Naming it in the first revelation to a society that transmitted by memory, and to a man who did not write, is one of the passage's sharpest details.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The cave sits on a hill about two miles from Mecca, up a steep climb, and it is small enough that a man inside it fills most of it. From the entrance you can see the town below. People used the hills around Mecca for retreat, and going out to one for days at a time with provisions was a recognised practice, not an eccentricity.
studies.didYouKnow: These are held to be the first ayat of the Quran ever revealed, and they sit near the end of the Book, in the ninety-sixth of a hundred and fourteen surahs. The order of revelation and the order of the text are different arrangements, and the Quran preserves the second while the tradition remembers the first.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The first word of revelation is a command about receiving rather than about believing, and the first attribute given is generosity. That sets the terms for everything after: the relationship opens with something being handed over. Placing the pen in the first five lines also gives writing a standing the culture had not, and the closing clause defines the human being by what he was taught rather than by what he knew.

crossReferences.why: Swears by the same instrument at the head of another early surah, giving writing the same weight.
Runs the identical pairing of teaching and creating, in the same order, at the opening of another surah.
Continues this surah immediately, naming what a person does with knowledge once he thinks he needs nothing.

studies.applyIt: Learn one small thing today that you did not know and will not use: the name of a tree on your street, how a word in your own language got there. The first command of the Quran is about receiving what you were not carrying, and doing it once with something useless keeps the habit honest.
